One greeting in an elevator led to a dinner and a deal.

Kevin explains how he stepped into a hotel elevator in Australia and greeted a businessman and his colleague by name. They had only met briefly at a party days earlier.

They were impressed. That led to a dinner invitation and then a business partnership that grew over the next couple of years.

Kevin's point: remembering names is not a parlor trick. It is real-world stuff that builds relationships.

When did remembering someone's name change how they treated you?
